facts.detail: The consumer USO guide was published on 8 August 2023.
The page was last updated on 20 March 2026.
Every UK home and business has a legal right to request a decent, affordable broadband connection.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Requests are made to BT, or KCOM in the Hull area.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and build cost.
Eligibility requires no coverage by a public broadband scheme in the next 12 months.
Network build or upgrade costs of £3,400 or less do not require a customer contribution.
For costs above £3,400, a survey and quote should be provided within 60 days.
Most connections should be delivered within 12 months, with some taking up to 24 months.

facts.detail: The codes-of-practice page was published on 28 April 2010.
The page was last updated on 16 July 2025.
Updated broadband speed codes apply to purchases from 21 December 2022.
Section 52 of the Communications Act 2003 underpins complaint-handling conditions.
General Condition C4 is the relevant complaints and dispute-resolution condition.
GC C4.2 requires provider complaint procedures to conform to Ofcom's approved code.
GC C4.3 requires providers to belong to an approved ADR scheme.
Non-compliance can lead to a penalty of up to ten percent of turnover.
The voluntary automatic-compensation scheme began on 1 April 2019.
The 2022 speed-code changes aligned the right to exit with revised General Conditions.

facts.detail: The business broadband code page was published on 25 January 2016.
The stated protections began on 30 September 2016.
Ofcom reported that one fifth of SMEs were dissatisfied with the speeds they received.
The code aims to provide accurate and transparent speed information at point of sale.
Providers should give expected download and upload estimates before purchase.
Relevant speed information should be provided in writing after sale.
Signatories must manage business speed problems and offer assistance.
Customers can exit without penalty if speed remains below the minimum guarantee after attempted resolution.
The code applies regardless of business size.
The code covers standard business broadband across ADSL, cable, FTTC, FTTP, wireless and satellite.

facts.detail: The consumer broadband-speeds guide was published on 21 November 2022.
The code requires clear speed information when a broadband service is purchased.
If a network speed problem cannot be fixed within 30 days, the provider must offer a penalty-free exit.
The page lists nine providers covered by the consumer protections.
Estimated speeds should cover 8-10pm for homes and 12-2pm for businesses.
Providers should give a personalised minimum guaranteed speed.
Ofcom recommends an ethernet-connected device for the most accurate speed test.
The right to exit applies to financially, contractually or technically linked bundled products.
Post-sale information should include speed estimates, relevant policies and problem steps.
ASA advertising rules require the average speed received by at least 50% of customers at the busiest time.
